blocks.text: A loose collection of cleaning functions, even reusable ones, is not the same as a real pipeline. A pipeline formalizes ORDER, makes each step independently testable, and lets the whole sequence be applied consistently to any new dataset with one call.

items: A defined, fixed ORDER of steps, since some cleaning operations depend on others already being done.
Each step takes the output of the previous step as its input, forming a clear chain.
The whole chain can be run, tested, and reasoned about as a single unit.

blocks.text: For example, type conversion should generally happen before range validation, since you cannot check if a value is in a valid numeric range while it is still stored as text.
4. Scikit-learn Pipeline as the Production Standard

scikit-learn Pipeline chains together a sequence of transformer objects, each implementing fit and transform methods. This is a more formal version of the same idea shown above, especially useful when the pipeline needs to be combined with a machine learning model at the end, a topic developed further in the Machine Learning Fundamentals course.

code.content:
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

pipeline = Pipeline([
    ('imputer', SimpleImputer(strategy='median')),
    ('scaler', StandardScaler()),
])
clean_array = pipeline.fit_transform(numeric_df)

blocks.title: A real ordering bug
blocks.content: Deduplicating BEFORE standardizing text casing can fail to catch duplicates that only look different because of casing, like "John Smith" and "john smith". Deduplicating AFTER normalization catches them correctly. Getting the order wrong causes a silent, hard to notice bug.

blocks.text: Since each step is just a function taking a dataframe and returning a dataframe, each one can be unit tested on a small, deliberately crafted input independent of the full pipeline, catching a bug in one step without needing to run the whole chain.

code.content:
def test_normalize_text():
    test_df = pd.DataFrame({'name': [' John ', 'JANE']})
    result = normalize_text(test_df)
    assert result['name'].tolist() == ['john', 'jane']

items: Putting steps in the wrong dependency order, as shown in the casing example above.
Building a pipeline that is not itself idempotent because one of its steps is not.
Tightly coupling a cleaning pipeline to one specific dataset column names, making it impossible to reuse on a new but similar dataset.
List every cleaning step and think through its true dependencies before fixing an order.
Type conversion before validation, normalization before deduplication.
Test each step independently on a small crafted input.
Consider scikit-learn Pipeline when the cleaning chain feeds directly into a model.
